hypotheses.justification: `_hprin` is mentioned nowhere else in the statement; the proof only passes it to the helper lemma `exists_entire_sub_polarPart_godementEisenstein_isUniformlySiegelBounded_fe_poles_of_mem_schwartzBruhat2`. It is always true by the product formula. In this theorem `α` is by definition the library's `moduleChar F` (`(NNReal.toRealHom.toMonoidHom.comp (distribHaarChar 𝔸)).toHomUnits`); the proof's `rfl` steps (`hEE`) confirm the two agree definitionally. `IsPrincipalTrivial α` unfolds to `∀ u : Fˣ, α (Units.map (algebraMap F 𝔸) u) = 1`. The library proves `NumberField.AdeleRing.distribHaarChar_algebraMap` (Theorems/Thm_NumberField_AdeleRing_distribHaarChar_algebraMap.lean): for any number field `F` with `[MeasurableSpace 𝔸] [BorelSpace 𝔸]`, both of which the theorem already has, and any `a : Fˣ`, `distribHaarChar 𝔸 (Units.map (algebraMap F 𝔸).toMonoidHom a) = 1`. Mathlib's `distribHaarChar` sets up its own Borel structure internally (`letI := borel A`), so it does not depend on the measurable-space instance in scope. Replacement proof, built inside the proof and passed to the helper lemma in place of `_hprin`: `fun u => Units.ext (by rw [val_moduleChar_apply, Units.val_one]; unfold NumberField.TateGlobal.ideleNorm; erw [NumberField.AdeleRing.distribHaarChar_algebraMap F u]; simp)`. The library already uses exactly this argument for F = ℚ, in S_AutomorphicForm_exists_rs22GlobalIntegral_..._rat.lean at lines 264–271. This general-F version has not been compiled, but nothing in the argument depends on F = ℚ. No degenerate case applies: F is a number field, so Fˣ is non-empty and the statement is never vacuous.
